title: GradMap: A Gradient-Descent Approach to Simultaneous Technology Mapping, Buffer Insertion, and Gate Sizing
problem: Technology mapping, buffer insertion, and gate sizing are traditionally sequential or use greedy approaches. This work addresses the need for simultaneous optimization of these interdependent tasks.
motivation: Simultaneous optimization of circuit design tasks can achieve better quality-of-results than sequential approaches.
method: Treats circuit design as a differentiable optimization problem—one where you can compute gradients like neural network training—then applies gradient descent to simultaneously optimize three interconnected choices: logic gate selection (technology mapping), repeater placement (buffer insertion), and transistor sizing (gate sizing). Since these choices affect each other—transistor sizes determine circuit speed, which determines where repeaters are needed, which constrains gate selection—optimizing them jointly finds better solutions than sequential tuning. The GPU-accelerated method efficiently explores the design space.
key_novelty: First to simultaneously optimize technology mapping, buffer insertion, and gate sizing using gradient descent on differentiable circuit timing analysis.
contributions: Differentiable STA formulation enabling gradient-based optimization
7-33% QoR improvements over state-of-the-art ABC tool
limitations: Limited to pre-synthesis stages; scalability on very large designs not discussed.
primary_theme: Simultaneous circuit optimization via differentiable STA
